key_challenges: Small test set prone to overfitting
Handling missing values and imbalanced target distribution

recommended_approaches.name: Robust Missing Value Handling
recommended_approaches.description: Impute missing values using predictive techniques (e.g., KNN imputation or model-based imputation). For categorical variables, use mode with a 'Missing' category. For numerical variables, use domain-specific imputation (e.g., age by Pclass/Sex).
recommended_approaches.rationale: Proper imputation reduces noise and prevents models from learning incorrect patterns. Small test sets require stable training data to avoid overfitting.

recommended_approaches.name: Feature Engineering for Interactions
recommended_approaches.description: Create features like 'Title' from names, 'FamilySize' (SibSp + Parch), and binned versions of age/fare. Extract cabin deck information if available. Add interaction terms (e.g., Pclass * Age).
recommended_approaches.rationale: These features capture meaningful patterns observed in similar competitions and help models generalize better on small test sets.

recommended_approaches.name: Ensemble of Simple Models
recommended_approaches.description: Combine predictions from Random Forest, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression using simple averaging or stacking. Use cross-validation to prevent overfitting.
recommended_approaches.rationale: Ensembling reduces variance and improves accuracy. Cross-validation ensures models generalize well to the small test set.

recommended_approaches.name: Class Weight Adjustment
recommended_approaches.description: Use class weights in models (e.g., XGBoost's scale_pos_weight) to address target imbalance. Consider SMOTE for oversampling minority classes during training.
recommended_approaches.rationale: Imbalanced data leads to biased models. Adjusting weights improves minority class recall, which indirectly boosts accuracy.

recommended_approaches.name: Regularization and Simplification
recommended_approaches.description: Apply L2 regularization in models like Logistic Regression and Random Forest. Simplify complex features if overfitting is detected during validation.
recommended_approaches.rationale: Regularization combats overfitting on small test sets. Simplification ensures models remain generalizable.

model_recommendations.name: Logistic Regression
model_recommendations.rationale: Simple, interpretable, and effective for small datasets with proper regularization to prevent overfitting.

model_recommendations.name: Decision Tree
model_recommendations.rationale: Handles small data well with explicit control over depth and pruning to avoid overfitting.

model_recommendations.name: k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)
model_recommendations.rationale: Non-parametric method suitable for small datasets when paired with careful hyperparameter tuning.

pitfalls.issue: Overfitting to the small test set
pitfalls.description: A small test set (~400 rows) increases the risk of models memorizing test patterns rather than generalizing, leading to inflated performance metrics that collapse in real-world scenarios.
pitfalls.mitigation: Use rigorous cross-validation (e.g., stratified k-fold) with the training data, apply regularization, and prioritize model simplicity.

pitfalls.issue: Data leakage from external historical records
pitfalls.description: Using external data (e.g., historical records) risks achieving artificially high scores by exploiting information not available in the competition's dataset, violating fairness and generalizability.
pitfalls.mitigation: Strictly use only the provided data; avoid any external sources unless explicitly permitted by competition rules.

pitfalls.issue: Metric gaming due to imbalanced classes
pitfalls.description: Imbalanced data may incentivize models to prioritize majority classes, leading to poor performance on underrepresented classes despite seemingly good overall metrics (e.g., accuracy).
pitfalls.mitigation: Use appropriate evaluation metrics (e.g., F1, AUC-ROC) and apply techniques like class weighting, resampling, or cost-sensitive learning.

pitfalls.description: Moderate missingness may contain meaningful patterns (e.g., missing not at random), but improper handling (e.g., naive imputation) can introduce bias or lose critical information.
pitfalls.mitigation: Analyze missingness mechanisms, use advanced imputation (e.g., MICE), and consider modeling missingness as a feature if justified.

pitfalls.description: The tutorial nature may encourage simplistic approaches (e.g., default models) that fail to address real-world complexities like data drift or feature engineering.
pitfalls.mitigation: Apply rigorous validation, experiment with feature engineering, and benchmark against diverse baselines.
